# Northstar — Monday Business Review Analysis

---

## 1. EXECUTIVE SUMMARY

**The business is shrinking on a net MRR basis despite positive headline numbers.**

Active MRR declined from **€746,100** at end-September to **€732,400** at end-October (–€13,700, –1.8%), because **€27,800/mo of churned MRR outpaced €14,100/mo of new bookings and expansions**. The October invoiced-revenue figure of €873,400 masks this decline — it is inflated by Gringotts' one-time annual billing (+€110,000 vs. a normal monthly invoice) and by four churned Starter customers who were still invoiced in October (€10,300).

Five customers churned in October. Four were SMB Starter (44% logo churn in a single month); one was Mid-market Pro (Nakatomi, €180,000 ARR). Meanwhile, **Wayne Enterprises renews on 30 November** — our second-largest customer at €1,008,000 ARR — with open high-severity support tickets.

October expansion bookings totalled **€216,000 annualized** across five Enterprise-plan customers, all attributed to paid search. These take effect in November's billing cycle and partially offset the churn losses — but only if Wayne renews.

**Gross margins by plan tell the real story:** Enterprise 29.5% (declining), Pro 62.7% (healthy), Starter 32.2% (low and getting worse with churn). The CFO's request for CAC payback by channel **cannot be answered** — there is no marketing-spend data in this pack.

The three leadership decisions should be resolved as follows:

| Decision | Recommendation |
|---|---|
| Reduce investment in a segment | **Yes — SMB Starter.** High churn, low margin, customers use less than half their included capacity. Stop acquiring and redirect resources. |
| Increase spend on one channel | **Not yet.** No cost data exists to evaluate ROI. Expansion attributions to paid search are inflated and causally questionable. |
| Which plan gets engineering focus | **Pro plan.** Best margins, clearest product issues (rate limits hitting overage customers), direct upsell revenue opportunity. |

---

## 2. REVENUE & CUSTOMER HEALTH

### 2.1 Invoiced Revenue vs. Underlying Run-Rate

| | September | October | Δ |
|---|---|---|---|
| Total invoiced revenue | €797,100 | €873,400¹ | +9.6% |
| Of which: Gringotts annual billing | — | €120,000 | one-time |
| Of which: Churned customers still billed | — | €10,300 | non-recurring |
| **"Steady-state" invoiced** | **€797,100** | **€753,100** | **–5.5%** |

¹ *Excludes the suspected duplicate soylent record (see §6).*

The headline +9.6% growth is an illusion. Stripping out Gringotts' annual pre-payment and revenue from customers who have already churned, invoiced revenue actually **fell 5.5%** month-over-month. November will be worse: Nakatomi (€15,000/mo) drops off, and the four churned Starter customers will no longer be billed.

### 2.2 MRR Bridge (Active Customers Only)

| Component | Monthly MRR impact |
|---|---|
| **Opening active MRR (end-Sep)** | **€746,100** |
| New logos: Spacely, Cogswell, Bishop, Gekko, Paper-Street | +€11,100 |
| Hooli expansion | +€3,000 |
| Nakatomi churn (Mid-market, Pro) | –€15,000 |
| Slate-Rock, Mega-Lo-Mart, Dinoco, Buy-N-Large churn (SMB, Starter) | –€10,300 |
| Soylent invoice decrease | –€2,500 |
| **Closing active MRR (end-Oct)** | **€732,400** |
| **Net change** | **–€13,700 (–1.8%)** |

The October bookings and expansions generated €14,100 of new MRR, but churn destroyed €27,800. **The business is on a net-negative growth trajectory.**

### 2.3 November Outlook (Projected)

October's acquisition.csv shows five expansion bookings (all Enterprise-plan customers) totalling €216,000 annualized = **€18,000/mo** of new MRR taking effect in November:

| Customer | Expansion MRR |
|---|---|
| Stark Industries | +€7,000 |
| Umbrella Health | +€4,000 |
| Globex | +€3,500 |
| Cyberdyne | +€2,000 |
| Massive Dynamic | +€1,500 |

Assuming no further churn and these expansions land:

| | Oct Active MRR | Nov Projected |
|---|---|---|
| Enterprise plan | €659,500 | €677,500 (+€18,000 from expansions) |
| Pro plan | €51,200 | €51,200 |
| Starter plan | €21,700 | €21,700 |
| **Total** | **€732,400** | **€750,400** |

This would recover to just above September — **but only if Wayne Enterprises renews on 30 November.** If Wayne does not renew, November MRR drops to **€666,400**, a –10.6% decline from October active and –10.7% from September. Wayne's renewal is the single largest risk in the business right now.

### 2.4 Wayne Enterprises — Renewal Risk Profile

| Signal | Detail |
|---|---|
| ARR | €1,008,000 (€84,000/mo) — 2nd largest customer |
| Renewal date | 30 November 2026 (5 weeks away) |
| Usage trend | +10% requests, +10% tokens — healthy |
| Support (Oct) | 4 tickets, including 1 high (api_errors, **resolved**) + 1 high (performance, **pending**) + 1 medium (integration, **open**) |
| Support (Sep) | 4 tickets, including 1 medium integration **still pending into October** |

Two high-severity tickets in October, one still pending. A medium integration ticket has been open since September. This customer has unresolved issues heading into renewal. **Immediate action required.**

### 2.5 Soylent — Distress Signals

| Signal | Detail |
|---|---|
| Segment / Plan | Mid-market, Enterprise plan |
| ARR | €234,000 (€19,500/mo) |
| Usage change | –27% requests (980K → 715K) |
| Revenue change | Invoice dropped from €22,000 to €19,500 |
| Support (Oct) | **8 tickets** (up from 3 in September), including 1 **critical** severity, 3 high, 1 high still **open** |
| Outstanding tickets | 1 high (api_errors) open; 1 medium (integration) pending |

Soylent is showing classic pre-churn behaviour: declining usage, increasing support volume, unresolved critical issues. At €234,000 ARR this is a significant risk.

### 2.6 SMB Starter — Churn Emergency

Four out of nine Starter customers churned in October:

| Customer | Tenure at churn | ARR | Sep → Oct requests |
|---|---|---|---|
| Slate-Rock | 21 months | €24,000 | 95K → 62K (–35%) |
| Mega-Lo-Mart | 18 months | €32,400 | 140K → 88K (–37%) |
| Dinoco | 12 months | €27,600 | 110K → 71K (–36%) |
| Buy-N-Large | 25 months | €39,600 | 165K → 104K (–37%) |

**Logo churn rate: 44% in one month. Revenue churn: €123,600 ARR.**

All four customers were using well below the Starter plan's 200,000 included requests. None triggered overage billing. Their usage was declining 35–37% in the month they churned. This pattern — customers paying for capacity they never use, then quietly disengaging over 3–6 months before cancelling — suggests a product-value problem, not a pricing or overage problem.

**Four new Starter customers were acquired in October** (Cogswell, Bishop, Gekko, Paper-Street), replacing the losses numerically. But new Starter MRR (€7,900/mo) is lower than churned Starter MRR (€10,300/mo). Net Starter MRR is negative.

### 2.7 Acme Migration — Not a Problem

Acme's requests fell 45% (4.2M → 2.31M), consistent with the documented batch migration. However, tokens only fell 12% (4,620M → 4,066M), meaning per-request token density increased. The actual computational load proxy (tokens) barely changed. Acme's ARR (€936,000) and invoice (€78,000/mo) are stable. This is an efficiency gain, not a risk.

---

## 3. ACQUISITION

### 3.1 Funnel Performance (Lead → Paid Trial)

| Channel | Sep Leads | Sep Conv. | Sep Rate | Oct Leads | Oct Conv. | Oct Rate | Trend |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Paid Search | 520 | 44 | 8.5% | 900 | 58 | 6.4% | ↓ Volume ↑, Rate ↓ |
| Content | 260 | 31 | 11.9% | 330 | 34 | 10.3% | Stable |
| Partner | 60 | 15 | 25.0% | 75 | 17 | 22.7% | Best rate, low volume |
| Outbound | 160 | 10 | 6.3% | 195 | 11 | 5.6% | Worst rate |

Paid Search dominates lead volume (+73% MoM) but its trial conversion rate dropped from 8.5% to 6.4%. The funnel only tracks lead → trial. **Trial → paid conversion data is not in this pack.** We cannot calculate end-to-end conversion or cost per acquired customer from these files.

### 3.2 Paid Conversions by Channel

| Channel | Sep New Logos | Sep Attr. Rev | Oct New Logos | Oct Attr. Rev | 2-Mo New Logo Rev |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Partner | 2 | €166,800 | 0 | — | €166,800 |
| Content | 1 | €45,600 | 2 | €45,600 | €91,200 |
| Outbound | 1 | €33,600 | 1 | €22,800 | €56,400 |
| Paid Search | 0 | — | 2 | €64,800 | €64,800 |

**Partner** delivered the highest new-logo revenue (€166,800) from just two September conversions — but had zero paid conversions in October. **Content** is the most consistent performer (two new logos each month, similar contract values). **Paid Search** acquired only two new-logo customers in two months despite the highest lead volume.

### 3.3 Expansion Attribution — A Caution

Paid Search also received attribution for five expansion bookings totalling €216,000 annualized in October (and one in September at €36,000). These are **existing customers** (Hooli, Stark, Umbrella, Globex, Massive-Dynamic, Cyberdyne) who expanded their contracts. The marketing platform credited Paid Search because a paid campaign was running when the expansion occurred.

This attribution is almost certainly **over-crediting Paid Search.** These are Enterprise-plan customers with direct sales relationships. The expansions likely reflect organic growth, sales team activity, or contract timing — not paid-search clicks. Including these in channel ROI calculations would overstate Paid Search's effectiveness.

### 3.4 CAC Payback by Channel (CFO's Request)

**This cannot be calculated.** The data pack contains:

- ✅ Leads, trial conversions, paid conversions, attributed revenue
- ❌ **Marketing spend by channel** (essential for CAC)
- ❌ Trial-to-paid conversion rates and timing (essential for cycle time)
- ❌ Sales team costs allocated to channels

Without cost data, any CAC or payback figure would be fabricated. **Recommendation: request channel-level spend data from marketing before the next review.**

## 4. PLAN ECONOMICS

### 4.1 Margin Summary

| Plan | Sep Revenue | Sep Infra | Sep Support | Sep Margin | **Sep Margin %** |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Enterprise | €659,000 | €288,000 | €159,000 | €212,000 | **32.2%** |
| Pro | €63,000 | €13,600 | €6,900 | €42,500 | **67.5%** |
| Starter | €24,100 | €8,400 | €7,300 | €8,400 | **34.9%** |
| **Total** | **€746,100** | **€310,000** | **€173,200** | **€262,900** | **35.2%** |

| Plan | Oct Revenue | Oct Infra | Oct Support | Oct Margin | **Oct Margin %** |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Enterprise | €659,500 | €296,800 | €168,000 | €194,700 | **29.5%** |
| Pro | €66,200 | €16,100 | €8,600 | €41,500 | **62.7%** |
| Starter | €32,000 | €11,400 | €10,300 | €10,300 | **32.2%** |
| **Total** | **€757,700** | **€324,300** | **€186,900** | **€246,500** | **32.5%** |

### 4.2 Enterprise Plan — Largest Revenue, Worst and Declining Margins

- Gross margin fell from 32.2% → 29.5% on essentially flat revenue (€659K → €659.5K).
- Infrastructure cost rose 3.1% (€288K → €296.8K) on **flat total request volume** (26.54M → 26.44M).
- Per-request infrastructure cost increased from €0.01085 to €0.01123 (+3.5%). This warrants investigation — it may reflect Acme's migration inefficiency, higher token density per request, or infrastructure pricing changes.
- Support cost rose €9,000 (+5.7%) per customer (€11,357 → €12,000).
- **Per-customer margin declined from €15,143 to €13,907 (–7.8%).**

Enterprise plan margins are eroding despite stable usage. The Acme migration has not yet delivered cost savings at the plan level. If enterprise infrastructure costs continue to grow faster than revenue, the core business margin will compress further.

### 4.3 Pro Plan — Best Margins, Clear Product Issues

- Gross margin at 62.7% — by far the strongest of any plan.
- Per-customer margin: €4,611 (Oct).
- **Three Pro-plan customers exceeded their 600,000 included-request cap in October:**

| Customer | Requests | Overage % | Rate-Limit Tickets (Oct) |
|---|---|---|---|
| Wonka Industries | 1,020,000 | +70% | 5 |
| Aperture Labs | 705,000 | +18% | 2 |
| Vandelay | 690,000 | +15% | 1 |
| Prestige Worldwide | 545,000 | –9% (approaching) | 2 |

Wonka Industries is generating **70% overage** and filed **five rate-limit support tickets** in October alone (four resolved, one open). At renewal, this overage will be billed separately, creating a potential revenue uplift — but the current rate-limiting experience is generating significant support burden.

If these overage customers upgraded to the Enterprise plan (or a higher Pro tier), the revenue impact would be substantial. Wonka at €4,200/mo on Pro would likely pay 2–3× on Enterprise.

### 4.4 Starter Plan — Low Margin, High Churn, Under-Utilized

- Gross margin: 32.2% (October), with per-customer margin of only **€792/mo**.
- Support cost per customer (€792/mo) nearly equals the per-customer margin (€792/mo). This means **almost all of the Starter margin is consumed by support.**
- Starter customers use an average of 84,385 requests against 200,000 included — **42% utilization.** No customer is anywhere near the overage threshold.
- These customers are paying for capacity they do not need, and the product is not delivering enough value to retain them.

**The Starter plan is structurally unprofitable when accounting for customer acquisition costs** (which are not in this data but must exist). Each churned Starter customer requires replacement to maintain the revenue line, creating a costly treadmill.

### 4.5 Plan-Level Summary

| Metric | Enterprise | Pro | Starter |
|---|---|---|---|
| Gross margin % | 29.5% ↓ | 62.7% | 32.2% ↓ |
| Revenue share | 87.0% | 6.8% | 4.2% |
| Customer count (Oct) | 14 | 9 | 13 (9 active) |
| Churn risk | Wayne renewal | Nakatomi lost | 44% monthly logo churn |
| Product issues | Infra cost growth | Rate limits, overage | Value delivery, activation |
| Upsell opportunity | Stark/Umbrella/Globex expansions booked | Wonka, Aperture, Vandelay overage | None visible |

---

## 5. RECOMMENDATIONS

### 5.1 Decision 1: Reduce Investment in SMB Starter — **YES, SUPPORTED BY DATA**

The data unambiguously supports de-prioritizing the Starter plan and SMB segment:

- **44% monthly logo churn** (4 of 9 customers)
- **Net-negative MRR contribution** (churned MRR exceeds new MRR)
- **Lowest per-customer margin** (€792/mo, almost entirely consumed by support)
- **Customers use <50% of included capacity** — the product is not delivering value
- New Starter acquisitions in October (4 customers, €7,900/mo MRR) only partially offset losses (€10,300/mo), and there is no evidence the new cohort will perform differently

**Specific actions:**
1. **Pause paid acquisition for Starter.** Stop spending marketing budget on a segment that churns at 44%/month. The CAC is unrecoverable.
2. **Redirect CS resources** from Starter to Enterprise (Wayne renewal, Soylent retention).
3. **Do NOT sunset existing Starter customers** — honour their contracts, but don't invest engineering cycles in Starter-specific features.
4. **Analyze churned Starter cohorts** (tenure, onboarding, activation metrics) to understand whether the product could be fixed for this segment or whether it's a fundamental market-fit issue. The 12–25 month tenure before churn suggests a lifecycle problem.

### 5.2 Decision 2: Increase Spend on One Acquisition Channel — **NOT YET, DATA INSUFFICIENT**

The data does not support increasing spend on any channel:

1. **No cost data exists.** Without marketing spend by channel, we cannot calculate ROI, CAC, or payback. Increasing spend without this data is a gamble.
2. **Paid Search conversion efficiency is declining.** Lead volume +73% but trial conversion rate dropped from 8.5% to 6.4%. Diminishing marginal returns are already visible. The headline attributed revenue is inflated by expansion bookings that are likely misattributed.
3. **Partner has the best conversion rate (23–25%)** but delivered zero paid conversions in October. It may have a scale ceiling.
4. **Content is the most consistent** new-logo performer across both months.

**Specific actions:**
1. **Request channel-level spend data** from marketing immediately. Until we have this, no spend increase should be approved.
2. **Investigate the trial-to-paid gap.** We know 92 leads reached paid trials in October but we don't know how many converted to paying customers. This is the critical missing metric.
3. **Challenge the expansion attribution model.** Five existing Enterprise customers expanding their contracts should not all be credited to Paid Search. Work with marketing to refine multi-touch attribution before making channel investment decisions.
4. **Explore scaling
